title: Make merge cleanup the default, on a real merge only
action: Decisions D1 and D1a. Cleanup runs unless --no-cleanup is passed or .bee/config.json sets worktree_cleanup_on_merge: false. Copy the config pattern verbatim from archive_on_close_enabled (close.rs:827): read_config_raw, then absent-or-non-false means ON, only a literal Bool(false) opts out. --cleanup stays ACCEPTED and becomes a no-op, so existing scripts keep working. FOUR THINGS THAT ARE DEFECTS IF SKIPPED: (1) --no-cleanup must join keys_known(&flags, &["id", "cleanup", "queue-wait-ms"]) at handlers.rs:386 or the entire merge returns None. (2) A non-boolean value on --no-cleanup is REFUSED outright -- not ignored, not delegated. bool_flag_true (handlers.rs:29) maps anything that is not the bare flag or the string 'true' to false, and bool_flag_ok's rejection path returns None which falls through try_native to a runtime that does not exist here. Today a mis-parsed cleanup flag means the favour was not done; after the flip a mis-parsed --no-cleanup means deleted anyway. Same care for the config key: the close.rs pattern reads a typo'd "no" string as ON, so validate the value and refuse a non-boolean rather than defaulting it. (3) handlers.rs:475 gates a holds-ledger read on `cleanup` and returns None on a corrupt ledger -- under the flip that fires on EVERY merge and lands on the router's unsupported-shape refusal. Fix the branch so a corrupt ledger degrades gracefully, and fix its comment ('only --cleanup can reach it'), which becomes a lie either way. (4) The ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE arm (phases.rs:240) routes the zero-work merge through the same attach_cleanup_outcome call as the green merge at phases.rs:393 -- it must KEEP today's behavior and remove nothing. Otherwise re-running merge to check status deletes the worktree, and a worktree holding an hour of uncommitted gitignored work reads as clean plus trivially merged. TEXT SURFACES that must move with the behavior or the CLI starts lying: cleanup_suggested_command (merge.rs:368) currently suggests --cleanup, which is backwards once cleanup is the default; the usage line at mod.rs:9; the worktree.merge description in the registry payload, which narrates the opt-in semantics at length (hand-edit per D5); a worktree_cleanup_on_merge row in docs/config-reference.md after the worktree_first row at :164, matching that table's format; and the key in .bee/config-sample.json beside worktree_first. Rename tests.rs:228 cleanup_without_the_flag_only_suggests to what it now tests -- the cleanup=false branch -- do not delete it.

truths: A merge with no flags cleans up
--no-cleanup leaves the worktree and branch standing
worktree_cleanup_on_merge false beats the absent flag
artifacts: The worktree_cleanup_on_merge row in docs/config-reference.md and the key in .bee/config-sample.json
prohibitions: Do not let cleanup run on the ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE arm
Do not let a non-boolean flag or config value resolve to clean-up
Do not remove the --cleanup flag -- it stays accepted as a no-op
Do not weaken the dirty-tree, conflict, or red-verify refusals

trace.outcome: Cleanup runs by default on a real merge; --no-cleanup and worktree_cleanup_on_merge:false opt out, non-boolean values refuse, ALREADY_UP_TO_DATE removes nothing
